newsitem.title: USA: Mexico coffee escapes frost damage - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: Mexico coffee escapes frost damage - Smith Barney.

text.p: Temperatures held above freezing in Mexico's coffee-growing areas Friday morning, sparing coffee trees from any frost-related damage, said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis.

Thick cloud cover prevented readings from dropping to critical levels in the northern fringes of the coffee belt, Davis said in a daily weather update, with lows recorded this morning from 36-44 degrees Fahrenheit.

Conditions will remain unseasonably cold through Saturday with the possibility of patchy frost in the northern reaches of the coffee zones, he said. But it was highly unlikely that significant crop damage would occur.
"Readings on Saturday morning are expected to be a bit cooler," he said. "Temps are not expected to drop to levels which would cause any major widespread damage, however."

By Sunday, the weather should begin to turn warmer, with normal readings expected during the first half of next week. Thermostats in the central U.S. are forecast to plunge again by mid-week as another cold front arrives, but the cold front should pass north of Mexico, Davis said.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
